{{short description|American herpetologist (born 1945)}}
[[File:USFWS - Harry Greene with tortoise, 2023 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Greene in 2023 with a [[Bolson tortoise]]]]
'''Harry W. Greene''' (born September 26, 1945) is an American [[herpetologist]], who retired in 2016 after working for many years as a professor of [[ecology]] and [[evolutionary biology]] at [[Cornell University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ecologyandevolution.cornell.edu/content/greenefest-honors-retiring-herpetologist-harry-greene|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161012230556/http://ecologyandevolution.cornell.edu/content/greenefest-honors-retiring-herpetologist-harry-greene|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 12, 2016|title='GreeneFest' honors retiring herpetologist Harry Greene {{!}} Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Cornell Arts & Sciences|website=ecologyandevolution.cornell.edu|access-date=2019-07-21}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Greene achieved a B.S. in Biology at [[Texas Wesleyan University]] in 1968, an M.A. in Biology from the [[University of Texas at Arlington]] in 1973, and a PhD in Zoology from the [[University of Tennessee]] in 1977. He worked as a US Army medic in Germany in 1968-1971.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.humansandnature.org/harry-w.-greene|title=Harry W. Greene|website=Center for Humans & Nature|language=en|access-date=2019-07-21}}</ref>

== Career ==
Greene has made many scientific publications (about 150 by 2005) and conducted field work in the United States, Europe, Mexico, Central America, South America, Africa and Vietnam. His main areas of research are evolutionary biology, behavioral and community ecology, vertebrate conservation, and feeding and defense in lizards and snakes. He was a researcher for one episode of the 2008 [[BBC]] series ''[[Life in Cold Blood]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://edgeeffects.net/harry-greene/|title=Rewilding and Reptiles: A Conversation With Naturalist Harry Greene|date=2015-05-05|website=Edge Effects|language=en-US|access-date=2019-07-21}}</ref>

Greene is the Stephen Weiss Presidential Fellow and Professor of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at Cornell University and the recipient of the [[E. O. Wilson]] Award from the [[American Society of Naturalists]].<ref name=":0" /> His book ''Snakes: The Evolution of Mystery in Nature'' (UC Press), won the [[PEN Literary Award]] and was a ''New York Times'' Notable Book.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/evolution/publications.php?pid=36015|title=Harry W. Greene - Publications|website=academictree.org|access-date=2019-07-21}}</ref>

== Books ==

*''Tracks and Shadows: Field Biology as Art'' (University of California Press, 2013); {{ISBN|978-0-520-23275-4}}
